regras.titulo: no hidden Markdown region addressed to an agent

porque.texto: GitHub renders a Markdown file with its HTML comments and unused link definitions removed, and an agent reads the raw file, so a sentence can reach the model that no reviewer saw on the page. Claude Code strips only block-level comments, and only from CLAUDE.md; Codex, Copilot, Cursor and the rest read instruction files raw. Elements hidden by a style or by the hidden attribute count too, because an editor preview that renders raw HTML hides them, and so does the MDX expression comment of an .mdx page. Code and comments are read in one pass, the way CommonMark gives the construct that starts first the text, and inside list items and block quotes too.

Hidden prose is common and honest (381 of 690 public instruction files that carry a comment hide prose in it), so a region counts only when it is addressed to an agent: a vocative, an override of earlier instructions, a request to conceal, a condition on being a model, a model that must act, or an imperative beside an execution token. Measured with the shipped engine: 0 regions in the local repositories, 0 in rebar, 0 in node_modules, and 2 regions in 2 of 690 public instruction files.

A heuristic because a signal is vocabulary: a first design that also counted an imperative next to an addressee fired on 3 honest local files. Its vocabulary is internal to the engine and not an exported table, a departure from how the other injection rules publish theirs: exported, its patterns would match rebar's own prose, and this rule never reads visible prose.

provas.porque: GitHub renders Markdown with its HTML comments removed and an agent reads the raw file, so a comment addressed to an agent is text the reviewer never saw. The fail side is an AGENTS.md whose block comment opens with a note for the coding agent (the vocative family). The pass side holds what honest repositories carry: the AGENTS.md rebar generates, rebar numbers markers around a count, a translator note in a comment with no addressee, and the same note for the agent inside a closed fence and inside a code span, where the page shows it. Drop the fence mask or the code span mask and the pass side goes red; drop the vocative family and the fail side goes green.

GitHub strips the hidden attribute, but the Markdown preview bundled with Cursor renders raw HTML with no sanitizer, so there an element with that attribute hides its text. The fail side is a README with a paragraph carrying the attribute and a condition on being an AI assistant; the pass side is the same paragraph without the attribute, visible everywhere. Stop reading hidden elements and the fail side goes green; treat every element as hidden and the pass side goes red.

A link reference definition nobody uses renders as nothing on GitHub, and the `[//]: # (...)` shape is the common way to write a Markdown comment. The fail side is a Copilot instructions file whose unused definition carries a title that opens by naming the assistant. The body of a definition is the label, a line break and the title: joined by a space, the title no longer starts the body, and the fail side goes green (measured). The pass side uses the same label in a later paragraph, so the definition is a real link target and not a hidden region: count used definitions and the pass side goes red.

Public instruction files wrap managed sections in namespaced marker comments of other tools. The pass side is a GEMINI.md whose markers start with the word agents followed by a colon, which the vocative family reads as addressing an agent: drop the generic marker shape and the pass side goes red. The fail side is a GEMINI.md with a comment that addresses Gemini by name, which no marker shape excuses.

The not-applicable branch: with no tracked Markdown and no agent rule file there is no page to hide anything in, and silence by absence must not become passed (invariant I4). The rule has one such branch, so both sides reach it by different trees: the pass side tracks one source file, the fail side tracks a text note and an agent JSON config, which carry no Markdown region. Return null there and both sides diverge.

In CommonMark a comment that starts a line and never closes runs to the end of the document, hidden. The fail side is a CLAUDE.md with a stray inline opener in a paragraph (literal text, not a comment) and then a line-start opener that never closes, followed by an override of earlier instructions. Stop at the stray inline opener, as the first prototype did, or require a closer, and the fail side goes green. The pass side has the same stray opener and the same lines inside a closed fence: drop the fence mask and it goes red.

regras.titulo: an AGENTS.md carrying the rebar generator marker matches a template rebar generated

porque.texto: The generator marks the AGENTS.md it writes. Until 2026-09-13 it trusted that marker anywhere in the file and copied a third-party Next.js block into it unread; it now keeps a marked file only when it equals the render, and warns on a block it does not know. To a reviewer the marker is still a claim, and one who sees it skips a file that may not be generated at all.

The whole root AGENTS.md is matched against every template version the generator ever rendered (5 so far, kept append-only in injection/moldes-agentes.json), with the project name, the Next.js block and, since the template pins it, the rebar commit as slots, and any tail allowed. It fails on a false claim: the marker below the top, repeated, in another instruction file, or no version matching. The 3 generated repositories match today, with no tail.

A heuristic for its first release, though an exact match is not a guess: it is promoted once a release shows it fails no honest project. An unknown block is a warning only when it is large or carries a URL, fenced code, a nested comment or an execution token.

provas.porque: The rebar generator marks the AGENTS.md it writes, and a reviewer who sees the marker skips the file. The pass side is the AGENTS.md the current template renders for a project, which matches the last version of the append-only template table. The fail side is the same file with one word of section 1 changed: the marker now claims a template no version matches. Drop the exact match and the fail side goes green; lose a version from the table and the pass side goes red.

The marker belongs only at the top of the root AGENTS.md, and a nested AGENTS.md is loaded by Codex, Copilot and Cursor for its folder. The fail side adds docs/AGENTS.md starting with the marker next to an exact root render. The pass side keeps docs/AGENTS.md without the marker and adds a Copilot instructions file that quotes the marker inside a fence: judge only the root file and the fail side goes green; count a fenced marker and the pass side goes red.

The generator writes its marker on the first line only, and the generator itself trusts the marker anywhere in the file. The fail side puts a heading above an otherwise exact render, so the marker is below the top; the pass side is the render. Accept the marker anywhere and the fail side goes green.

The generator writes its marker once. The fail side appends a second marker to an exact render. The pass side appends the marker inside a fenced code block that documents it, which is shown as code and claims nothing: count the marker inside code and the pass side goes red; stop counting and the fail side goes green.

The not-applicable branch: when no instruction file carries the marker there is no claim to hold (invariant I4). Both sides reach it for different reasons. The pass side is a hand-written AGENTS.md with no marker. The fail side has a Markdown file that starts with the marker but is no instruction file (docs/template.md, which no client loads), the way rebar tracks its own template: read every Markdown file and the fail side stops being na.

Projects generated by an older template keep matching: rebar-site tracks a version-3 AGENTS.md byte for byte. The pass side is the version-3 render with a Next.js block for that project name, and the block is small, has no URL, fence, nested comment or execution token, so its unknown hash is no warning. Compare only against the current template and the pass side goes red. The fail side is the same render with one literal line extended, which matches no version.

regras.titulo: no URL, host, package name or config identifier mixing writing systems

porque.texto: One letter from another alphabet turns a host or a package name into a different one that reads the same: Daniel Stenberg showed an AI-written report for curl on 2025-05-16 whose GitHub link began with an Armenian letter, and CVE-2021-42694 is the identifier form. A model copies the address; a reviewer reads the familiar name.

Judged with the UTS #39 resolved script set at the Highly Restrictive level, over URL hosts (punycode labels decoded, the host as one token), URL segments, package manifest names and agent config keys and identifier values. Measured 0 mixed tokens in about 450,000 of them across the local repositories and node_modules.

Never prose or code identifiers: the same test over every word hit 92 honest words in 4 local repositories. A heuristic because an honest internationalized host under a Latin top-level domain mixes too.

provas.porque: The curl project received an AI-written report whose GitHub link began with an Armenian letter in place of the g. The fail side is a README with that link. The pass side holds the honest non-ASCII a repository carries: the same link in ASCII, a Portuguese accented path segment, a Japanese path segment on a Latin host, and a resistance written with the Greek omega in prose, which is never judged. Judge prose, or treat any non-ASCII as mixed, and the pass side goes red; judge only the path and the fail side goes green.

An MCP server name that reads like a known one is how a lookalike server gets approved. The fail side is a .mcp.json whose server key has a Cyrillic i inside it; the pass side is the same file in ASCII. Stop reading agent config keys and the fail side goes green.

The not-applicable branch: with no URL, no package manifest and no agent config there is no token to judge (invariant I4). Both sides reach it by different trees: the pass side tracks a text note with no address, the fail side tracks nothing and has no commit. Return null there and both sides diverge.

A dependency name with one Cyrillic letter installs a different package than the one a reviewer reads. The fail side is a package.json whose dependency key has a Cyrillic a in place of the Latin one; the pass side is the same manifest in ASCII. Stop reading dependency keys and the fail side goes green.

A host written in punycode is plain ASCII in the file and a different name once the client decodes it. The fail side links a host whose punycode label decodes to a Latin name with one Cyrillic letter; the pass side links a German host whose label decodes to Latin letters only. Skip punycode decoding and the fail side goes green; judge the encoded label as foreign and the pass side goes red.

regras.titulo: no script that gained a download or shell pipe, no Python module shadowing the standard library

porque.texto: An instruction file says to run the tests and the agent obeys, so the injection can change what the tests run instead of touching the instruction file: GitInject measured the configuration-file channel working where a pull request body did not.

Two signals fail. Since the first parent of HEAD, a package script that changed and gained an execution family (a pipe into a shell, a download, a URL that leaves the machine, eval called and the like). And any tracked Python module, in any suffix the import system loads, named like a standard library module where a script run by path would import it first. A new script npm runs on install with no family only warns: 258 of 1,261 node_modules manifests with scripts carry one, and none of their 261 hooks carries a family.

"A script an instruction file names changed" alone fired on 14 of 212 honest commits; the refined signal on 0 of 200 changed script values. The Python signal hit 4 of 19,927 importable files of an installed site-packages. A heuristic because an honest change can add a download to a script, and a folder of scripts can hold a module named like the standard library on purpose.

provas.porque: A script run by path puts its own folder first on the import path, so a file there named like a standard library module is what the script imports. The fail side tracks a scripts folder with a json module file next to a script that imports json. The pass side keeps that module inside a package folder with an __init__.py, the precision trade-off the rule makes. Stop judging Python file names and the fail side goes green; drop the package exemption and the pass side goes red.

The not-applicable branch: a manifest whose repository has no parent commit gives no range to judge, and with no Python file there is no static half either (invariant I4). Both sides track a package.json with a postinstall script and reach it by different routes: the pass side has no commit at all (an unborn branch), the fail side has one root commit. Evaluate the range against an empty parent and both sides report the hook as new.

A folder with an __init__.py named like a standard library package shadows that package for a script run from its parent folder. The fail side tracks a logging package at the repository root; the pass side keeps the same package inside an app package, whose parent has an __init__.py. Stop judging package folders and the fail side goes green.

regras.titulo: the rebar MCP server a tracked config launches is a version rebar shipped

porque.texto: The client starts `.rebar/mcp.mjs` on every session, and headless sessions start project servers without asking. mcp-server-launch pins the launch text, `node .rebar/mcp.mjs`, and nothing pinned the file it names: an edit to the server walked past every rule while the launch never changed.

So the tracked blob must be byte for byte a version of the template rebar generates, looked up by sha256 in a table derived from rebar's git history. A table and not the running template, because rebar-site tracks version 2 (blob 8bc5d7f) and assay and navesz-portfolio track version 6 (blob ea75237): all three would fail against the current file for code rebar wrote. The current version passes, an older one passes with a note on how to update, an unknown one fails. Version 1 fails too although rebar shipped it: it runs npx --yes github:Navesz/rebar --mcp, unpinned, every time the client starts it, and a review measured a downgrade to it passing every rule.
No allowlist entry, because the honest way to run a modified server already exists: launch it under another file name and accept that launch by fingerprint.

provas.porque: An MCP client starts the file a tracked config launches on every session, and the launch text of .mcp.json never changes when that file does. Both sides track the template .mcp.json. The pass side tracks .rebar/mcp.mjs as version 2 of rebar's template (blob 8bc5d7f, 45,574 bytes, what rebar-site tracks), a blob no later commit can change, so the case never ages and it passes with the update note; the fail side tracks version 1 (blob 6cf8634, 10,416 bytes), a launcher rebar shipped that runs npx --yes github:Navesz/rebar --mcp, unpinned, every time the client starts it. Whoever judges the launch and not the bytes, or accepts every version rebar ever shipped, turns the fail side green; whoever accepts only the current template turns the pass side red, and with it rebar-site and assay, which track versions 2 and 6. Unknown bytes fail in mcp-integrity__not-applicable.

A tracked .rebar/mcp.mjs that no MCP configuration launches is a file no client starts, so the rule has nothing to judge and must say not applicable (invariant I4). The pass side tracks only an unknown server file with no config and must be na; the fail side is the base failing tree, a config launching unknown bytes. Whoever judges every tracked .rebar/mcp.mjs turns the pass side red.

A config that launches a file git does not track runs whatever sits on disk, which no review saw. Both sides track the template .mcp.json; the pass side also tracks version 2 of the server (blob 8bc5d7f), the fail side tracks no server at all. Whoever returns not applicable when the launched file is missing from the index turns the fail side green.

regras.titulo: no workflow, MCP config, package script or agent instruction runs a git or tarball package without a commit pin

porque.texto: A branch, a tag or no ref at all runs whatever the remote repository holds at the instant the job starts, so a push there changes what this repository executes with no diff here. rebar's own generated projects ran the ruler that way until 2026-09-13, three sites at once.

The fix has to be a spelling the runner accepts. Measured on 2026-09-13: npm 10.9.3, the npm of Node 22 on the CI runners, exits 1 on a git spec with a commit ref, and npm 10.9.3 and npm 11.6.2 both run the commit tarball from codeload. So a 40-hex commit passes as a git ref or as a codeload or archive tarball, and so does a registry tarball with an exact version.

Workflows, MCP launches, package.json scripts and agent instruction files are judged, because each runs a command no person retypes; an agent executes what its instructions tell it to. Prose is not: rebar's README carries 5 command lines that run rebar unpinned for the people who read it (measured on 2026-09-13). No allowlist entry, because an entry would pin the text and the text keeps running whatever the branch holds next.

provas.porque: A workflow step that runs a GitHub package with no ref runs whatever the default branch holds when the job starts. The fail side runs the package by its bare owner/repo spec; the pass side runs the commit tarball from codeload, the spelling npm 10.9.3 (Node 22 on the runners) accepts where it refuses a git spec with a commit ref, measured on 2026-09-13. Whoever reads the tarball as unpinned turns the pass side red; whoever skips workflows turns the fail side green.

A commented line does not execute. The pass side keeps the unpinned step as a YAML comment above a pinned run; the fail side has the same step uncommented. Whoever reads the raw text of a workflow turns the pass side red.

A folded YAML scalar joins its lines into one command, so the runner and its package may sit on different lines of the file. The fail side folds an unpinned run over two lines; the pass side folds the pinned tarball. Whoever judges each line apart turns the fail side green.

A branch name after the hash is still a moving target; only a 40-hex commit id cannot move. The fail side pins the git spec to main, the pass side to a 40-hex commit. Whoever accepts any ref as a pin turns the fail side green; whoever refuses a commit ref turns the pass side red.

An agent runs the command its instruction file tells it to run, and a README command is read by a person before it is typed. The fail side puts an unpinned run in a fenced block of AGENTS.md; the pass side puts the same fenced block in README.md, next to a pinned workflow. Whoever judges prose turns the pass side red, and rebar's own README, whose quick start runs rebar unpinned on 5 lines, with it; whoever skips instruction files turns the fail side green.

An MCP server launched from a GitHub package with no commit changes what every session starts whenever that branch moves, and an allowlist fingerprint pins only the launch text. The fail side launches the package by its bare spec; the pass side launches it by a 40-hex commit. Whoever reads only workflows turns the fail side green.

A repository with no workflow, MCP config, package script or agent instruction file has nothing this rule reads, and silence by absence must not become passed (invariant I4). The pass side tracks only a README and must be na; the fail side is the base failing workflow. Whoever returns null there turns the pass side into a divergence.

A package.json script runs on npm run with no one retyping it, so an unpinned remote package there moves with the branch. The fail side has a script that runs a GitHub package with no ref; the pass side runs a registry package by exact version, which this rule does not judge. Whoever skips package scripts turns the fail side green; whoever judges registry versions as git specs turns the pass side red.

A run step written as a quoted YAML scalar is the same command: measured, a line reader split it into one word and saw no runner. The fail side quotes an unpinned run; the pass side quotes the pinned tarball. Whoever reads workflows line by line instead of parsing the scalar turns the fail side green.

decisoesFechadas.decisao: The `site` preset is pure SSG: `output: "export"` and `images.unoptimized`. No server, and that is why the og:image exists for whoever does not execute JavaScript.
porque: Pure SSG. It is what makes og:image exist: WhatsApp, LinkedIn, Slack and Discord do not execute JavaScript, so a meta tag painted on the client does not exist for them. Measured in the 31/08 spike — every route "prerendered as static content", out/index.html at 12 KB and the absolute meta inside it.
